To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CR3 regions of adenovirus 3, 5 and 40 interact with pCAF in a manner that contributes to transcriptional activation.

we have identified a novel, previously unrecognized binding site for the acetyltransferase pCAF in the adenovirus EIA protein and have shown that this binding site is important for transcriptional activation by the CR3 region of E1A.
the HAdV E1A proteins bind the acetyltransferase pCAF through two independent sites and that pCAF contributes to E1A mediated transcriptional activation in human cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of transcriptional activation of early adenoviral genes by the adenovirus type 5 E1 protein.
the identification of a second independent acetyltransferase binding site in the HAdV CR3 region of E1A that contributes to the transcriptional activity of CR3.
the identification and characterization of the cellular proteins that interact with adenovirus EIA proteins and how these proteins contribute to the regulation of viral gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pCAF acetylates the CR3 portion of the E1A protein and that this acetylation is important for the function of the E1a protein in the viral life cycle.
CR3 interacts with pCAF and that this interaction is required for CR3 dependent transcription.
CR3 of E1A interacts with the pCAF protein, a member of the SAG-A complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HAdV E1A CR3 regions are potent activators of transcription in yeast and mammalian cells and that this activity is dependent on interaction with pCAF.
the CR3 portion of HAdV E1A proteins interacts with pCAF, a component of the transcriptional regulatory SAGA complex, to promote expression of viral early gene transcription.
the CR3 region of the HAdVs 5, 12 and E3-9 E1A proteins interact with pCAF and that pCAF is required for the transcriptional activation activity of the CR3 region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pCAF acyltransferase is a key component of the E1A transcriptional regulatory machinery.
